zh.summary: Ambio 是一家总部位于赫尔辛基的 AI 原生再生塑料采购平台，为欧洲塑料加工商提供经过验证的再生聚合物材料、结构化质量数据与端到端供应链服务。
zh.judgment: Ambio 的核心商业判断是：再生塑料的采用瓶颈不在材料本身，而在质量可预测性与采购信任，因此用 AI 驱动的批次测试数据与匹配报价系统替代传统静态数据表和分散的贸易商网络。
zh.replaces: 替代传统再生塑料贸易中依赖静态数据表、人工询价和分散供应商的采购流程，以及塑料加工商自行筛选和验证再生料质量的内部工作。
zh.segment: AI 驱动的再生塑料采购与质量验证平台，属于可持续材料供应链科技方向。
zh.product: Ambio 提供 AI 原生的端到端再生塑料采购解决方案，覆盖 rLDPE、rHDPE、rPP、rPVC、rPA、rABS、rPS、rPC 等多种再生聚合物牌号。其核心能力包括：将加工商的生产要求翻译为材料属性、匹配已认证的再生料牌号、对每批交付进行测试并与生产要求比对、以及提供结构化的批次历史质量数据。公司还运营回收商合作伙伴网络，为回收商对接欧洲塑料加工商的经常性需求。官网展示了 rPA 的详细技术文档，涵盖物理、机械、化学性质、应用场景和常见问题。
zh.customer: 使用者是欧洲塑料加工商（converters），他们需要为注塑、吹塑、挤出等工艺采购再生聚合物；付费者同样是这些加工商，按采购的再生材料付费。回收商是供应侧合作伙伴，通过 Ambio 获得客户、合同和物流服务。核心痛点是再生塑料批次间质量波动大、缺乏可靠的质量数据、采购流程分散且信任成本高，导致加工商难以将再生料纳入稳定生产。
zh.workflow: 流程分为四步：第一，加工商提交生产要求，Ambio 将其翻译为材料属性并筛选匹配的已认证材料；第二，Ambio 展示最佳匹配牌号，附带价格和质量数据，供客户选择或测试多个牌号；第三，Ambio 为每批交付制定测试计划并安排货运，确保材料按时按约定到达工厂；第四，客户可选择现货采购或转为合同采购，建立长期供应关系。整个流程从需求输入到交付由 Ambio 作为单一责任方协调。
zh.business_model: Ambio 通过向塑料加工商销售再生材料获取收入，客户可现货采购或签订长期合同。官网未披露具体定价、加价率或佣金结构。单位经济推断：收入可能来自材料销售差价或服务费，但具体模式未披露，需标注为推断。回收商侧可能通过需求匹配和物流服务参与分成，但同样未披露。
zh.traction: 公司披露其销售覆盖 DACH、北欧、芬兰与波罗的海、法国等市场，每个市场有指定销售联系人。官网列出了加工商最常订购的牌号，并展示了 rLDPE 批次历史示例。融资方面，公司于 2026 年 10 月完成 510 万欧元种子轮，投资方包括 Lifeline Ventures、b2venture 和 Montis Capital。缺失证据：未披露客户数量、收入、留存率、具体交付量或案例研究。
zh.moat: 与通用 AI 模型相比，Ambio 的壁垒在于其积累的批次级质量数据、认证的回收商网络和与加工商建立的采购关系。通用模型无法提供经过实际测试的再生料性能数据或承担供应链责任。与旧流程相比，Ambio 用动态批次数据替代静态数据表，降低了加工商的验证成本。壁垒条件：数据网络效应需要足够多的交付批次和回收商参与才能形成，且需持续证明其质量预测的准确性。
zh.funding_read: 种子轮融资表明投资者认可其将 AI 应用于再生塑料采购的方向，资金可能用于扩展材料品类、增加销售覆盖和建设数据基础设施。但资金用途未披露，下一里程碑可能是证明客户留存、扩大交付量或进入新市场。融资本身不构成需求验证或产品胜出的证据。
zh.risks: 第一，再生塑料质量波动可能超出 AI 匹配和测试计划的控制范围，导致客户生产中断或退货，损害信任。第二，回收商网络扩展可能受限于合格回收商的稀缺性和地域分散性，导致供应不稳定。第三，加工商可能因价格或惯性继续使用原生塑料，再生料采用速度低于预期。第四，若无法证明批次数据能持续降低客户验证成本，客户可能回归传统贸易商。
zh.takeaway: Ambio 的做法表明，在材料供应链中，AI 的价值不在于替代材料本身，而在于将非标准化的质量信息结构化，降低交易双方的信任成本。创业者可借鉴：用数据服务嵌入实体交易，成为单一责任方，而非仅做信息匹配。
zh.watch_next: 可验证的下一指标包括：客户留存率与合同采购占比、交付批次数量与增长率、回收商合作伙伴数量、以及是否披露具体客户案例或收入数据。关键问题是：Ambio 的批次数据能否持续准确预测材料在客户生产线上的表现。

en.summary: Ambio is a Helsinki-based AI-native end-to-end procurement platform for recycled plastics, supplying verified recycled polymer materials with structured quality data and supply chain services to European plastic converters.
en.judgment: Ambio's core commercial bet is that the bottleneck for recycled plastics adoption is not the material itself but quality predictability and procurement trust, so it replaces static datasheets and fragmented trader networks with AI-driven batch testing data and a matching/quoting system.
en.replaces: Replaces traditional recycled plastics trading workflows that rely on static datasheets, manual quoting, and fragmented suppliers, as well as converters' internal efforts to screen and validate recycled material quality.
en.segment: AI-driven recycled plastics procurement and quality verification platform, within sustainable materials supply chain technology.
en.product: Ambio offers an AI-native end-to-end procurement solution for recycled plastics, covering grades such as rLDPE, rHDPE, rPP, rPVC, rPA, rABS, rPS, and rPC. Core capabilities include translating converter requirements into material properties, matching qualified recycled grades, testing each delivery against production requirements, and providing structured batch history quality data. The company also operates a recycler partner network, connecting recyclers with recurring demand from European plastic converters. Its website includes detailed technical documentation for rPA, covering physical, mechanical, and chemical properties, applications, and FAQs.
en.customer: Users are European plastic converters who need to procure recycled polymers for injection molding, blow molding, and extrusion; payers are the same converters, paying for the recycled materials they purchase. Recyclers are supply-side partners who gain customers, contracts, and freight services through Ambio. The core pain point is high batch-to-batch quality variability in recycled plastics, lack of reliable quality data, and fragmented procurement with high trust costs, making it difficult for converters to integrate recycled materials into stable production.
en.workflow: The process has four steps: first, converters submit production requirements, and Ambio translates them into material properties and screens qualified materials for the best fit. Second, Ambio presents best-matching grades with price and quality data, allowing customers to choose one or test several. Third, Ambio sets a test plan for each delivery and arranges freight, ensuring material reaches the plant on schedule and as agreed. Fourth, customers can buy on a spot basis or move to contract purchasing to build long-term supply relationships. Ambio acts as the single accountable party from requirement input to delivery.
en.business_model: Ambio generates revenue by selling recycled materials to plastic converters, who can purchase on a spot basis or sign long-term contracts. Specific pricing, markup, or commission structures are not disclosed on the website. Unit economics inference: revenue may come from material sales margin or service fees, but the exact model is undisclosed and should be labeled as inference. Recyclers may participate through demand matching and logistics services, but this is also undisclosed.
en.traction: The company discloses sales coverage in DACH, Scandinavia, Finland & Baltics, and France, with named sales contacts per market. The website lists grades converters most often order and shows an example rLDPE batch history. On funding, the company raised €5.1 million in a seed round in October 2026, with investors including Lifeline Ventures, b2venture, and Montis Capital. Missing evidence: no customer count, revenue, retention rate, specific delivery volumes, or case studies are disclosed.
en.moat: Compared to general-purpose AI models, Ambio's moat lies in its accumulated batch-level quality data, qualified recycler network, and procurement relationships with converters. General models cannot provide tested recycled material performance data or assume supply chain responsibility. Compared to legacy processes, Ambio replaces static datasheets with dynamic batch data, reducing converters' validation costs. Moat conditions: data network effects require sufficient delivery batches and recycler participation, and it must continuously prove the accuracy of its quality predictions.
en.funding_read: The seed round indicates investor recognition of applying AI to recycled plastics procurement, with funds likely intended for expanding material categories, increasing sales coverage, and building data infrastructure. However, the use of funds is undisclosed, and the next milestone may be proving customer retention, scaling delivery volumes, or entering new markets. Funding itself does not constitute demand validation or evidence of product success.
en.risks: First, recycled plastics quality variability may exceed the control of AI matching and test plans, causing production disruptions or returns and damaging trust. Second, recycler network expansion may be limited by the scarcity and geographic dispersion of qualified recyclers, leading to supply instability. Third, converters may continue using virgin plastics due to price or inertia, slowing recycled material adoption. Fourth, if batch data cannot consistently reduce customer validation costs, customers may revert to traditional traders.
en.takeaway: Ambio's approach shows that in materials supply chains, AI's value is not replacing the material itself but structuring non-standard quality information to reduce trust costs for both parties. Entrepreneurs can learn to embed data services into physical transactions and become a single accountable party, rather than just an information matchmaker.
en.watch_next: Verifiable next indicators include: customer retention and contract purchasing share, delivery batch volume and growth rate, number of recycler partners, and whether specific customer cases or revenue data are disclosed. The key question is whether Ambio's batch data can consistently and accurately predict material performance on customer production lines.

Recycled PA (rPA): properties, applications and benefits Materials we offer Ambio for Recyclers About us Request a quote Menu Materials we offer Ambio for Recyclers About us Request a quote Recycled polyamide (rPA): properties, applications and benefits Can PA be recycled? Yes. Recycled Polyamide (rPA) is an engineering thermoplastic recovered from post-consumer (PCR) and post-industrial (PIR) waste, such as production scrap, carpet fibre, fishing nets and automotive parts. It keeps virgin polyamide's strength, wear resistance and heat resistance. The common grades are PA6 and PA66 (PA6.6), often glass-filled for technical parts. Request a quote What are the key properties of recycled PA? Physical properties of rPA Unfilled recycled PA has a density of about 1.13 to 1.15 g/cm³; glass-filled grades are heavier. Polyamide absorbs moisture, which changes its stiffness and toughness and means it must be dried before processing. Mechanical properties of rPA rPA offers high tensile strength, toughness, fatigue resistance and excellent abrasion resistance. Dry, unfilled PA can be notch sensitive; conditioned or impact-modified grades are tougher. PA66 is stiffer and more heat resistant than PA6, and glass fibre raises both further. Chemical properties of rPA Recycled PA resists oils, greases, fuels and many solvents, but is attacked by strong acids. PA66 melts at around 260 °C and PA6 at around 220 °C, so both work at elevated temperatures. Frederik Sieler DACH +49 151 22276751 frederik.sieler @ambiomaterials.com Henrik Öhman Scandinavia +46 724511735 henrik.ohman @ambiomaterials.com Lumi Maunuvaara Finland & Baltics +358 503716746 lumi.maunuvaara @ambiomaterials.com Fiona Durand France +33 7 75 77 05 99 fiona.durand@ambiomaterials.com OR Request a quote What are common applications of recycled PA? rPA is available as granulate and compounds, mostly for injection moulding, with some extrusion and fibre spinning. rPA in automotive Automotive uses glass-filled PA for engine covers, air intake parts, brackets, housings, pedals, clips and fasteners, and connectors. Recycled PA6 and PA66 compounds serve many of these parts; the most demanding under-the-hood components need tightly specified, heat-stabilised grades, which is where batch testing matters most. rPA in textiles and fibres Textiles use rPA in sportswear, swimwear, hosiery and carpet fibre, much of it regenerated from nets and fibre waste. rPA in consumer and industrial goods rPA goes into power tool and appliance housings, furniture parts, gears, rollers, bearings and other wear parts. What are the benefits of using recycled PA? Environmental benefits rPA reduces waste and greenhouse gas emissions compared with virgin polyamide, whose production is energy intensive, and keeps material such as nets and fibre out of landfill and the sea. Economic benefits Recycled PA can cost less than virgin PA for the same part, and helps manufacturers meet recycled-content targets. Performance benefits Compounding with glass fibre, impact modifiers, heat stabilisers and flame retardants tunes rPA for demanding applications. PA6, PA66 and nylon What is the difference between PA6 and PA66? PA66 has a higher melting point, stiffness and heat resistance, suiting high-temperature parts. PA6 is easier to process, slightly tougher and usually cheaper. What is the difference between PA and nylon? They are the same family: nylon is a common trade name for polyamides. PA covers PA6, PA66 and others, used both as fibres and as engineering plastics. Request a quote Frequently asked questions about recycled PA How does recycled PA compare to virgin PA? Good rPA compounds perform similarly to virgin PA in many applications. Quality depends on feedstock, processing and compounding, and on moisture control. What are the challenges of using recycled PA? Moisture absorption, variation between batches and degradation from prior processing. Drying, restabilising and batch testing address them. Can recycled PA be recycled again? Yes, several times, though properties change gradually over repeated cycles. Is recycled PA toxic? Recycled PA is considered safe under normal use, though traces of additives or residual monomers may be present. Testing and compliance with REACH keep it within safety requirements. Is recycled PA biodegradable? No. Like virgin polyamide, it does not readily break down; recycling extends its lifespan. Where can I buy recycled PA?
